summary.title: Cosmos 3: Omnimodal World Models for Physical AI

details: Physical AI currently requires stitching together separate model classes (VLMs for perception/planning, video generators / forward-dynamics world models for simulation, VLA/world-action models for control), which is fragmented and computationally wasteful.
Understanding and generation are argued to be mutually dependent, so they should be learned in one model.

Cosmos 3: a family of open omnimodal world models that jointly process and generate language, image, video, audio, and action, with action treated as a first-class token modality via a unified SE(3) pseudo-action interface (ego pose deltas, effector pose deltas, grasp states) with domain-specific input/output projections.

Core mechanism: a Mixture-of-Transformers backbone in which every decoder layer holds two parameter sets — an autoregressive 'reasoner' tower (causal attention, next-token prediction) and a diffusion 'generator' tower (bidirectional rectified-flow denoising) — coupled by dual-stream joint attention where diffusion tokens attend to AR tokens but never vice versa; a single token-arrangement convention (AR prefix, then clean conditioning, then noisy targets ordered vision/audio/action) makes T2I, T2V(+audio), I2V/V2V, video transfer, forward/inverse dynamics, and policy all the same model without architectural change.

Enabling design: 3D MRoPE extended with absolute temporal modulation (temporal increment scaled by base-TPS/TPS) so video, audio, and action tokens at different frame/sampling rates share one physical time axis, plus a fixed large temporal gap between AR and diffusion subsequences.
Three scales: Edge (4B total, 2B dense trunk trained from scratch), Nano (16B, from Qwen3-VL-8B), Super (64B, from Qwen3-VL-32B); Nano and Super released.
Understanding path: ViT with 16x16 patches, 2x2 token merge, DeepStack feature aggregation, interleaved text timestamps; trained jointly with backbone.

Generation path: frozen Wan2.2-TI2V-5B video VAE (4x temporal, 32x32 spatial), frozen ETTA-style stereo 48 kHz audio VAE (25 tokens/s); linear projections into hidden dim; both towers initialized from the pretrained VLM weights.
AR-to-diffusion positional temporal gap set to 15000; base TPS = 6 (24 FPS / 4).

Reasoner: two-epoch multimodal pretraining (next-token prediction, <=16k tokens, sqrt-normalized per-token loss, AdamW lr 5e-5 LLM / 5e-6 ViT) then SFT (8200 steps, batch 512, importance-weighted mixture with 1:4 pretrain:SFT replay plus 800K instruction samples).

Generator: initialized from trained reasoner with reasoner tower frozen; rectified flow-matching velocity regression with per-modality noise sampling (mode sampling for video, logit-normal for image/audio/action) and resolution-adaptive shift (s=1/3/5 at 256p/480p/720p).
Multi-resolution multi-task pretraining across 256p/480p/720p, five aspect ratios, up to 400/300 frames, token packing at 74k tokens; task mix T2I/T2V/I2V/V2V = 20/56/16/8%.
Compute: Nano 31.05T pretraining tokens on 1024 GB200 GPUs; Super 17.86T on 2048 GB200; mid-training 2.4T (Nano) and 1.9T (Super) tokens.

Mid-training adds 15.6M curated images and 74.7M curated clips (robotics, driving, human activity, physics, synthetic), action data (forward/inverse dynamics, joint policy) with 10x action loss scale, and control-conditioned transfer (edge, blur, depth, segmentation, driving world-scenario maps).
Cosmos3-Super-Text2Image: two-stage SFT (20k steps on mixture 45% real / 40% synthetic / 15% text-rendering, then 2k steps on 470k ultra-high-quality pairs), 70k context, >720p images only.

Cosmos3-Super-Image2Video: 10k iterations, ~50B tokens, lr 1e-5, 480p / 189 frames (~8s at 24fps), agentically retrieved weak-spot data plus 1k manual and ~20k synthetic clips, 20% T2I tokens retained.

Cosmos3-Nano-Policy-DROID: resumed from mid-trained Nano with fresh action encoder/decoder (5x lr multiplier, lr 2e-4); DROID (76k trajectories, 86 tasks, 564 scenes) at 360x640 with idle-frame/failure filtering; 3-view 540x640 canvas plus proprioception; predicts 32 absolute joint positions at 15Hz with auxiliary RGB frames; inference with 4 diffusion steps, shift 5, CFG scale 3, video decoding skipped, served on 2 RTX Pro 6000 GPUs.

Structured JSON captions (not free-form) produced by in-house LoRA-finetuned Qwen3-VL-8B captioners; images annotated via quadrant-plus-center scan, videos with a second temporal-dynamics pass (actions, state changes, segments, transitions, camera motion, audio description).

Inference uses the Cosmos 3 Reasoner (or Claude for some post-trained models) as prompt upsampler filling the same JSON schema, plus long structured negative prompts and a video-transfer system-prompt prefix.
Infrastructure spans data curation to WebDataset, large-scale training, serving, and a unified benchmarking framework; released Cosmos-HUE benchmark and five synthetic datasets under OpenMDW-1.1.

key_findings.finding: A single MoT model with an AR reasoner tower and a diffusion generator tower can cover VLM understanding, image/video/audio generation, control transfer, forward and inverse dynamics, and policy learning without architectural modification.
key_findings.evidence: All modes are realized purely by token arrangement (AR prefix, clean conditioning, noisy targets) over shared decoder layers with dual-stream joint attention; the paper reports state-of-the-art or highly competitive results across the resulting understanding and generation benchmark suite summarized in the results overview table.

key_findings.finding: Post-training the omnimodal base yields best-in-class open-weight specialists, indicating the unified backbone is an effective starting point rather than a compromise.
key_findings.evidence: Cosmos3-Super-Text2Image scores 91.36 overall on UniGenBench (best among evaluated models) and ranked top-1 open-weight on the Artificial Analysis Text-to-Image leaderboard; Cosmos3-Super-Image2Video ranked top-1 open-weight on the Artificial Analysis Image-to-Video leaderboard.

key_findings.finding: The mid-trained omnimodal world model transfers to real robot control, becoming a leading policy model after lightweight action post-training.
key_findings.evidence: Cosmos3-Nano-Policy-DROID (32-action chunks at 15Hz, 4 diffusion steps, video decoding skipped) ranked first on RoboLab, RoboArena, and MolmoSpaces at submission time.

key_findings.finding: Absolute temporal modulation of 3D MRoPE is needed to align modalities with different sampling rates on one physical time axis.
key_findings.evidence: Temporal increments are scaled as base-TPS/TPS (video TPS = FPS/4, audio TPS ~25 from 48kHz with 1920 hop, action TPS = sampling rate), enabling synchronous video/audio/action generation across heterogeneous frame rates; FPS and duration are also injected into the prompt.

key_findings.finding: Adjacent positional indices at the text-to-vision boundary cause visual artifacts, fixed by a large positional buffer rather than new parameters.
key_findings.evidence: Starting diffusion tokens at the last AR token's temporal offset produced over-saturation and checkerboard artifacts in initial frames, most pronounced in the Super model; inserting a fixed temporal gap of 15000 removed the problem without architectural or learnable additions.
